elements.content: Communication Goal: I can talk about future plans, goals, and steps, and combine present, past, and future in one conversation.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0-A1 General English
- Unit: Inspired Module 8. Next Steps
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Next Steps
- Materials: Calendar visuals, goal icons, sequence cards, trip plan prompts.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use going to for plans
• express wants and needs with reasons
• sequence a plan and synthesise present, past, and future
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles present simple, past simple, and free-time vocabulary.

Next lesson: End of the inspired track. Recycles the full A0-A1 range in a now-then-next conversation.

Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (15 items):

tomorrow — the day after today. Example: I'm going to travel tomorrow.
next week — the week after this week. Example: I'm going to travel next week.
tonight — this evening or night. Example: I'm going to book the ticket tonight.
soon — in a short time. Example: I'm going to start soon.
plan — an idea about what you will do. Example: What is your plan?
start — to begin. Example: I'm going to start a new course.
learn — to get new knowledge or skill. Example: I want to learn English.
save — to keep money for later. Example: I need to save money.
move — to go to a new home or place. Example: I'm going to move to a new flat.
visit — to go and see a person or place. Example: I'm going to visit my family.
goal — something you want to achieve. Example: My goal is to speak more English.
skill — an ability to do something. Example: Speaking is an important skill.
language — a system of words for communication. Example: English is a global language.
healthy — good for your body. Example: I want to eat healthy food.
balance — a good mix of different things. Example: I need a better work-life balance.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I'm going to visit my cousin next month. (future plan)
• Are you going to take a break this summer? (future question)
• I want to speak more fluently because I talk to international clients. (want + reason)
• I need to sleep earlier this month. (need + time)
• First, I'm going to book the train. Then, I'm going to find a hotel. (sequencing)
• After that, we're meeting for dinner. (sequence marker)
• Usually I work late, last week I took a day off, and next week I'm going to start a project. (now-then-next synthesis)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the day after today'?
Which word means 'the week after this week'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Going to reduction and sequence stress

going to /ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə/ — natural reduction in speech
tomorrow /təˈmɒrəʊ/ — stress the second syllable
goal /ɡəʊl/ — long /əʊ/
finally /ˈfaɪnəli/ — three syllables
Listen and repeat:
I'm going to visit my family. First, I'm going to book the ticket. Then, I'm going to pack. Finally, I'm going to travel.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'be going to' to talk about plans and intentions for the future.

Form:
Going to: Subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb. Negative: isn't / aren't going to. Question: Are you going to...?

Examples:
• I am going to travel next month.
• She is going to visit her family.
• We aren't going to stay at home.
• Are you going to come to the party?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I ___ going to visit my family.
She ___ going to travel.
They ___ going to celebrate.
___ you going to come?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I am going to ... (travel / visit / study) ...
• She is going to ...
• We aren't going to ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What are you going to do this weekend?
• Where are you going to travel next year?
• Who are you going to visit?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your future plans with 'going to'.
• Write three sentences about a friend's future plans.
Reading: Next Steps

Sofia is going to start a new job next month. She wants to improve her English because she is going to lead weekly calls with clients in London. First, she is going to review her notes every morning. Then, she is going to practise speaking with a language partner twice a week. Tariq is going to hike in the mountains this summer. He needs to get fit because they are going to walk fifteen kilometres every day. First, he is going to buy good hiking shoes. After that, he is going to run three times a week.
Why does Sofia want to improve her English?
options: She is going to lead calls with clients in London.
She is going to move to London.

elements.content: What is Tariq's first step?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

I'm really excited about next weekend because I'm going to visit Amsterdam for three days. First, tonight I'm going to book my museum tickets online. Then, on Thursday evening, I'm going to pack a small backpack. Next, on Friday morning, I'm going to take the 8:15 train. Finally, when I arrive, I'm going to rent a bike and explore the canals.
What is the first step?
How is the speaker going to explore the city?
Speaking task: Share two goals and one plan. Ask one clarifying question for each goal.

• What are you going to do next month?
• What do you want to improve?
• What do you need to do?
• What is your first step?
• What did you do last week, and what are you going to do next?
Role-play: You are planning a trip or project with a partner. Agree on the first, next, and final step, and explain why.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write a six-sentence now-then-next plan: one current habit, one recent past event, one goal, and three sequenced steps.
Model: Usually I ... Last week I ... Next month I'm going to ... First, ... Then, ... Finally, ...
